show: The Bible in a Year (with Fr. Mike Schmitz)

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: Reflecting on Jeremiah's warnings against idolatry and Ezekiel's detailed temple vision.
kurzfassung: Father Mike Schmitz guides listeners through Jeremiah's teachings on idolatry and the human tendency to stray from God. The episode also explores Ezekiel's vision of the measuring of the temple and how early Christian writers interpreted these Old Testament texts through the lens of the New Testament. Additionally, a brief reading from Proverbs highlights the contrast between wisdom and foolishness.
stichpunkte: Reading from Jeremiah 10 and 11, Ezekiel 40, and Proverbs 15
Jeremiah emphasizes that giving hearts and minds to idols makes people foolish
Jeremiah acknowledges that human steps cannot be directed without the Lord's guidance and correction
Jeremiah faces intense opposition and conspiracies from the people of Jerusalem
Ezekiel chapter 40 begins an eight-chapter description detailing the construction and measurements of the temple
Gregory the Great's homilies provide a spiritual, New Testament interpretation of Ezekiel's temple gates
St. Augustine noted that the Old Testament is revealed in the New, and the New is hidden in the Old

clips.hook: Like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter
clips.text: Jeremiah recounts how he was targeted by plots against his life while remaining unaware of the conspiracies surrounding him.

clips.hook: Measuring the north gate and its stairway
clips.text: Ezekiel records the precise measurements and architectural details of the inner court gates.

clips.hook: A fool despises his father's instruction
clips.text: Proverbs contrasts the rejection of parental guidance by fools with the wisdom of accepting correction.

clips.hook: The way of man is not in himself
clips.text: Father Mike Schmitz reflects on human limitations and connects repentance to abandoning self-reliance in favor of God.

clips.hook: Spiritual meanings of the temple gates
clips.text: A commentary analyzes the symbolic meaning of the temple gates, linking specific directions to spiritual states like sinfulness and fervent virtue.

beschreibung:
Fr. Mike shows us from our reading of Jeremiah that when we give our hearts and minds over to idols we become foolish. The way of man is not in himself, we need the Lord to guide and correct us. In Ezekiel, we read about the vision of the measuring of the temple and Fr. Mike shows us how the early Church Fathers would read the Old Testament in light of the New Testament. Today’s readings are Jeremiah 10-11, Ezekiel 40, and Proverbs 15:5-8.

For the complete reading plan, visit ascensionpress.com/bibleinayear.
